datasource_item.source_question_text:
7. A Chinook salmon can jump out of water with a speed v0 and an angle 𝜃 above the horizontal. What is the speed of the fish when it is at the maximum height?
A. 𝑣0.
B. 𝑣0 cos 𝜃.
C. 𝑣0 sin 𝜃.
D. 0.
datasource_item.generated_question_text:
Q7. A ball is launched from level ground with initial speed $v_0$ at an angle $\theta$ above the horizontal (ignore air resistance). What is the ball’s speed at its maximum height?
A. $v_0$
This is incorrect because the vertical component of velocity decreases to zero at the top, reducing the speed.
B. $v_0 \cos \theta$
This is correct because at maximum height $v_y = 0$ while the horizontal component remains $v_x = v_0 \cos \theta$.
C. $v_0 \sin \theta$
This is incorrect because $v_0 \sin \theta$ is the initial vertical component, not the remaining speed at the top.
D. 0
This is incorrect because only the vertical velocity becomes zero; the horizontal velocity generally remains nonzero.

This is incorrect because adding components (4 + 7) is not the same as computing Euclidean distance.
D. None of the above is correct.

D. 7.5 m/s
This is incorrect because it comes from dividing momentum by the ball’s mass instead of the combined mass.
